messages.text: Hamilton apologises to Ferrari for overriding strategy call

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team for his costly decision to override their strategy call during the Singapore Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton apologises to Ferrari for costly decision to override strategy call during Singapore GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lewis Hamilton apologises to Ferrari for costly decision to override strategy call during Singapore GP Lewis Hamilton dropped from third to sixth in the Singapore Grand Prix after choosing not to pit under a Virtual Safety Car; Hamilton was called into the pits by his Ferrari team but opted to stay out; the seven-time world champion required medical checks as he felt unwell after the race Sunday 11 October 2026 16:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team for his strategy call, which cost them points at the Singapore Grand Prix Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team for his costly decision to override their strategy call during the Singapore Grand Prix. Hamilton was running in third behind his team-mate Charles Leclerc on the 39th of 62 laps when a Virtual Safety Car appeared to give him the perfect opportunity to change tyres after he had been the first driver to stop earlier in the race. Ferrari told Hamilton to follow Leclerc into the pits, but he ignored the call and stayed out, which resulted in him finishing the race sixth as he was overtaken by Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri in the closing stages. messages.text: Verstappen claims dominant first Singapore GP win

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time in his Formula 1 career with a dominant victory, while Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton endured a messy race strategically to tumble off the podium late on.
metadata.content: Singapore GP: Max Verstappen wins event for first time in F1 career ahead of Charles Leclerc as Lewis Hamilton apologises for strategy | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Singapore GP: Max Verstappen wins event for first time in F1 career ahead of Charles Leclerc as Lewis Hamilton apologises for strategy Red Bull's Max Verstappen dominated the Singapore Grand Prix with a lights-to-flag victory; Charles Leclerc was second and Kimi Antonelli third; Lewis Hamilton apologised for a messy race strategically that saw him finish down in sixth Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 11 October 2026 15:42, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix for the first time in his Formula 1 career with a dominant victory, while Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton endured a messy race strategically to tumble off the podium late on. Verstappen led every lap on his way to a second consecutive win despite being unable to communicate with the team due to a radio problem, but it did not affect him as he held off an early challenge from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc who eventually finished seven seconds behind in second. Kimi Antonelli took advantage of an elbows-out battle late on between Hamilton and McLaren's Lando Norris, with the seven-time world champion on old tyres in the latter stages, to take third and extend his lead over George Russell to 102 points in the Drivers' Champions

messages.text: Zheng stuns Andreeva to become first Chinese winner of China Open

metadata.summary: Olympic champion Qinwen Zheng made history as the ‌first Chinese player to win the China Open on Sunday, stunning French ‌Open winner Mirra Andreeva 7-5 6-4.

Wild card ​Zheng, who has been on a recovery path after missing nearly six ​months due to an elbow ‌injury on her dominant right arm, looked like her ​old self as she used powerful forehands to control the rallies, and landed swift ​winners angling away from Andreeva. After ⁠the two exchanged early ⁠breaks, world No 5 Andreeva held firm to go 5-4 ‌up, and almost got a decisive break when Zheng sent a cross-court shot too ‌long before netting a forehand. messages.text: Yamashita wins Korea Championship with course-record finish

metadata.summary: Miyu Yamashita put on a show on the final day of the LET's Aramco Korea Championship, firing a course record of 63 (-9) to win by three strokes with a total of 22 under par.
metadata.content: Aramco Korea Championship: Miyu Yamashita produces course-record finish to clinch Ladies European Tour title | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Aramco Korea Championship: Miyu Yamashita produces course-record finish to clinch Ladies European Tour title Ladies European Tour's Aramco Korea Championship sees Japan's Miyu Yamashita produce course record on final day to clinch title ahead of Czech Republic's Sara Kouskova; title is Yamashita's second title on LET, having also won the 2025 AIG Women's Open Sunday 11 October 2026 11:35, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final round of the Aramco Korea Championship Miyu Yamashita put on a show on the final day of the LET's Aramco Korea Championship, firing a course record of 63 (-9) to win by three strokes with a total of 22 under par. The world No 5 led from the 36-hole mark and was bogey-free once again at New Korea Country Club. Yamashita began well with birdies on the third, fifth, eighth and 10th holes to put herself in a good position with seven holes to go. However, the Czech Republic's Sara Kouskova was hot on her heels, but the 25-year-old major champion rolled in three birdies in four holes before making an eagle on 17 to seal her fourth win of 2026. It was the Japanese star's second title on the Ladies European Tour (LET), having also won the 2025 AIG Women's Open. messages.text: Brennan holds on for one-shot victory at Baycurrent Classic in Japan

metadata.summary: Michael Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic for his second victory of the season and third on the PGA Tour, parring the final six holes for a three-under 68 and a one-stroke margin over Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell.
metadata.content: Baycurrent Classic: Michael Brennan holds on to win title in Japan ahead of Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Baycurrent Classic: Michael Brennan holds on to win title in Japan ahead of Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell American Michael Brennan holds off challenges of compatriots Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell to clinch PGA Tour's Baycurrent Classic in Japan with victory; Win is Brennan's second title of season and third in his career; England's Jordan Smith finished three shots off the top Sunday 11 October 2026 08:45, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final round of the PGA Tour Baycurrent Classic Michael Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic for his second victory of the season and third on the PGA Tour, parring the final six holes for a three-under 68 and a one-stroke margin over Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell. Tied for the third-round lead with Bridgeman and Zach Bauchou in the FedEx Cup Fall event, Brennan rebounded from a bogey on the 10th with birdies on holes 11 and 12 before the winning par run at hilly Yokohama Country Club. His best par save came on the par-3 16th when he hit a long shot from a greenside bunker to a foot. He finished at 16-under 268.
